title: observability-token-kv-enhanced-metrics-dashboard-alerts
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Enhances token/KV observability: new dashboards for token-level cost & latency breakdowns, KV cache hit/miss tracing, and tuned alert thresholds to reduce noise while preserving SLO coverage. Backwards-compatible metrics and rollout by feature flag.
description: Context: customer telemetry and internal canaries show increased alert noise for token-level cost/latency and KV cache regressions during high-multiplex traffic. This PR centralizes token/KV observability, adds detailed dashboard panels, improves span tagging for KV cache events, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce false positives without losing SLO coverage. Motivation: reduce pager fatigue for on-call while preserving rapid detection of real regressions (ENG-2411, ENG-3012). Summary of changes: - New dashboards: token_cost_latency_kv_overview (Grafana) and token_kv_tracing_view (Tempo + Jaeger-style views). Panels include percentile token-latency by model, per-route token cost breakdown, KV cache hit/miss rate with tagging by request route/customer_tier, and per-GPU aggregate token throughput. - Metrics changes: add redwood.token.latency_p50/p90/p99, redwood.token.cost_per_token (sampled), redwood.kv.cache_hit{,ratio,route,model,tier}, and redwood.kv.operation.latency histograms. All metrics are emitted with existing common labels (model, route, region) to stay compatible with downstream rules. - Tracing changes: KV cache spans include new attributes kv.cache_key_hash (anonymized), kv.hit boolean, kv.size_bytes, and fast-path indicators to better correlate cost spikes. - Alert tuning: reduced sensitivity on low-cardinality signals and moved to aggregated-slo based alerts. Added three new alerts: TokenCostSpikes_Aggregate (rolling 5m p95 > baseline*2), KVMissRate_Elevated (sustained >5% over 10m for heavy routes), and TokenLatency_Regression (p99 increase >25% over baseline for >5m). - Dashboards: added templating (model, route, region, tier), better panel descriptions, and links to runbook sections. - Rollout: feature-flag guarded metrics and dashboards for gradual rollout; dashboards deployed to staging then prod; alerts soft-enabled (notify-team but not page for first 24h). Testing and validation: unit tests for metric emission, integration tests for tracing attributes, end-to-end dashboard smoke checks, and staged canary rollout against perf-canary cluster. Checklist: - [x] Metrics instrumentation added + unit tests - [x] Tracing attributes added + integration tests - [x] Grafana dashboards created and validated in staging - [x] Alerts added and tuned in Alertmanager/Prometheus - [x] Runbook updated and linked - [x] Feature flag gating for initial rollout Files changed (high level): dashboards/grafana/token_cost_latency_kv_overview.json, dashboards/grafana/token_kv_tracing_view.json, services/serving/runtime/metrics/token_metrics.go, services/serving/runtime/kv/kv_tracing.go, observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml, docs/observability/token_kv_observability.md, tests/integration/test_token_metrics.py, tests/e2e/dashboard_smoke_test.py. Backwards compatibility: metrics use existing label sets and new metric names avoid breaking existing alert rules; alerts are added but default to notify only during staging. Rollout plan: staged by region (us-west -> us-east -> eu-west) with feature flag flips and monitoring windows.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall looks good — big +1 for the runbook links. Two asks: (1) can we avoid emitting token.cost for every request (sample?), and (2) ensure kv.cache_key_hash is anonymized before instrumentation to avoid PII?

Evelyn Chen (author): Replied — token.cost is sampled at 1% by default via our sampling helper; added config and tests. kv.cache_key_hash is hashed with SHA256 and truncated; added comment + unit test for PII protection.

Liam O'Connor: Alert thresholds look reasonable but suggest moving KVMissRate_Elevated threshold to 5% for heavy routes and 10% for light routes (templated alert). Updated alerts to include route-weighting labels.
Maya Singh: Noted a potential perf hotspot in token_metrics emitter under high concurrency — suggested using a lock-free ring buffer. Implemented a bounded channel buffer and microbenchmark included.
Diego Morales: CI flake on dashboard json validation — observed schema error due to deprecated panel type; fixed and reran CI.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e dashboard smoke (initially failed due to deprecated panel, fixed in commit f4d2a2c and re-ran), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). Total runs: 3 (1 rerun for dashboard validation). Final status: pass.
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 by Diego Morales. Squash commit message: 'observability: token/KV enhanced metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning (ENG-2411, ENG-3012)'. Rollout started 2026-03-01 03:00 UTC to staging. Alerts soft-enabled for 24h, then fully enabled pending no regressions.
notes: Follow-up work: (1) Add automated baseline recalculation job for p95/p99 baselines (ENG-3105), (2) Add sampling knobs to the hosted API sidecar for token.cost to tune telemetry load, (3) Investigate per-customer alert suppression to reduce noisy tenants.
